reflections.title: "Bear the Iniquity of the Holy Things"

reflect.text: When we look honestly at our worship and service, we find that even our best moments are stained by sin. In church, during private prayer, or while helping others, our minds wander, and our hearts grow cold or proud. Sometimes we want others to admire how faithful we seem, or we serve out of habit rather than real love. Even our desire to weed out bad habits can come from selfish pride rather than true devotion.

God knew that our worship would never be completely pure on its own. For Israel, Aaron wore a golden plate engraved with God's holiness so that the people's offerings would be acceptable. Today, Jesus serves as our great High Priest. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, Jesus presents before the Father "not our unholiness, but his own holiness." He carries away the flaws in our worship and covers us with His perfect goodness.

questions: When have you noticed pride or distracted thoughts creeping into your prayers or worship?
How does knowing Jesus covers the flaws in your spiritual life give you peace when you come to God?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for loving us even when our worship and good works are mixed with selfish motives. We are grateful that Jesus stands before You as our High Priest, offering His own perfection in place of our weakness. Help us rest in His grace today. Amen.

reflections.title: Garments of Sweetness and Service

reflect.text: The clothing made for the priest was rich with meaning. Along the hem of the blue robe hung alternating golden bells and pomegranates. Like the lower hem of that robe, we may hold a humble place, yet God's Spirit still reaches us. When God blesses us, He calls us to show both sweetness and fruitfulness. The bells remind us to be gentle, cheerful, and kind to those closest to us, even when we feel tired from serving. The pomegranates remind us that true faith is not just emotional talk; it produces real, lasting fruit that helps others grow.

On his forehead, the priest also wore a gold plate engraved with the words that declared him holy to the Lord. This visible sign showed everyone that he belonged to God. As believers, we are marked by the Holy Spirit in every part of our lives. Carrying God's name means thinking carefully about how our words, moods, and actions affect the people around us. Instead of hiding what we believe, we can let Christ's kindness and light show plainly through how we treat others each day.

questions: Are you showing the sweetness of Christ to your family and friends, especially when you are tired?
How can the way you react to everyday challenges show others that you belong to God?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for giving us Your Holy Spirit and marking us as Your own. Help us to be both sweet and fruitful in how we live each day. May our words, actions, and attitudes reflect Your love and bring glory to You. Amen.
